items.content:
US tech is generating record gains for foreign institutional investors:

Norway’s $2.3 trillion sovereign wealth fund, the world’s largest, generated a record +$184.3 billion in profit in H1 2026.

This comes as the fund returned +9.4% over the period, while its 72.1% equity allocation was up +13.0%.

The AI revolution is boosting investment portfolios far beyond America.

items.content:
Tech sector breadth is rapidly improving:

75% of S&P 500 technology sector stocks finished above their 200-day moving average last week, the highest percentage since October 2024.

This marked the first time in 219 trading days that this threshold was reached, ending the 9th-longest streak on record.

By comparison, the longest stretch during which fewer than 75% of tech stocks traded above their 200-day moving average lasted 759 trading days, ending on April 22, 2003, following the Dot-Com Bubble burst.

Historically, each time such a streak ended, the technology sector returned +2.5% on average over the following month and +7.3% over the next 3 months.

After 6 months and 12 months, the average gains were +15.5% and +33.4%, respectively.

Meanwhile, 69% of Nasdaq 100 stocks are now trading above their 200-day moving average, near the highest percentage since July 2025.

The tech stock rally is gaining momentum.
— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) Aug 13, 2026

items.title: BREAKING: The US Government officially posts its largest July budget deficit in history, at -$432 billion, due to an acceleration in federal spending. Interest on US debt rose +$26 billion from last July's levels to an alarming $118 billion for the month. This puts total interest expense for FY2026 up to $1.17 trillion in FY2026. As a result, interest expense has officially surpassed both National Defense and Medicare spending. In other words, the US government now spends more money just on interest than it does to fund the entire US Military or to provide healthcare for seniors. We cannot afford higher interest rates.

items.title: Shocking stat of the day: Estimated annualized interest expense on US federal debt is up to a record $1.38 trillion. This is equivalent to 4.2% of US GDP, the highest percentage since 1997. By comparison, this figure stood at 2.3% in Q4 2020. Annualized interest expense has surged +$900 billion, or nearly +200%, over the last 5 years, rising at an average annual rate of +24%. Meanwhile, in the first 9 months of FY2026, interest expense jumped +$78 billion YoY, to $827 billion, the highest level for this period in history. The cost of servicing US federal debt has never been higher.

items.title: Employment in the US financial industry is going through a prolonged downturn: The financial industry shed -14,000 jobs in July, to 9.09 million, the lowest since July 2022. This marks the 5th consecutive monthly decline, totaling -59,000. Since May 2025, financial industry payrolls have dropped -121,000, posting the largest drawdown since the 2020 pandemic. Excluding the pandemic, this is the biggest employment contraction in the sector since the 2008 Financial Crisis. The decline comes as financial firms accelerate AI adoption, aiming to boost productivity and reduce labor costs across the industry. AI is reshaping the future of employment in finance.
